Description

About Chexy

At Chexy, we're building modern financial tools for Canadians, starting with their largest expenses. We turned rent, mortgages, tuition, insurance and other big bills into opportunities to earn rewards, improve cash flow and get more from money they already have to spend.

We're the first platform in Canada that lets people pay nearly any bill with a credit card while unlocking cashback, points and financial flexibility. Billions in payments move through Chexy, our customer base is growing fast, and we've just relaunched the brand. Over the next 12 months we launch several new products, starting with our first credit card in Q1 2027.

We're backed by Khosla Ventures, Crossbeam Venture Partners and Venrex, and we partner with Aeroplan and other leading Canadian financial and telecom brands.

About the role

Chexy is hiring a Manager, Partner Marketing to own the partner channel in market: turning our partnerships with Aeroplan and other leading Canadian financial and telecom brands into offers, campaigns and placements that bring in customers. You report to the CMO. This is an individual contributor seat; you run the channel yourself.

The commercial deal is done before it reaches you. Your job starts at the signature: what we and the partner put in market, when, with which offer, in whose channels, and what it produced. That means a co-marketing calendar across every partner, the partner offers themselves (welcome offers, points boosts, cardholder promotions, co-funded referral offers) and the partner-side approvals that get them live.

The other half of the job is the partners. You are the day-to-day relationship for their marketing and account teams: the plan, the assets, the reporting, the quarterly review and the ask for the next placement. Partners should hear from you before they have to ask.

You run on agents. Partner reporting, approval and asset tracking, and first drafts of decks, briefs and partner email copy are done by agents you build. Your time goes to partners, the calendar and what goes live next.

We care about taste, speed and results.

What you'll own

Partner go-to-market

• Every partnership from signed to live: the launch plan, the offer, the assets, the partner's approvals and the date

• A co-marketing calendar across all partners: who is in market when, with what, so partner moments land on top of our launches rather than against them

• Partner offers end to end: mechanics, terms, the landing page (with the Senior Brand Designer) and the handoff to lifecycle for the existing base

Partner channels

• Placements in partners' channels: emails, app and web placements, cardholder communications, events and content

• Co-branded pages and the creative partners run on our behalf, inside their brand rules and ours

Partner relationships

• The day-to-day relationship with each partner's marketing and account teams: the plan, the asks, the follow-through

• Partner reporting: a monthly performance read and a quarterly review every partner gets without asking, and the case for the next placement

• What partners' customers need to see before they sign up, fed back to brand and product

Pipeline

• The next co-marketing partners: loyalty programs, card issuers, telcos and the brands our customers already pay through Chexy. You find and qualify them and build the case; commercial terms are closed with the CMO and the founders

Measurement

• Partner-sourced signups, activation and CAC per partner and per campaign, against what paid delivers

• The monthly partner read to the CMO: what worked, what didn't, what's next

Agents

• Your own agents: partner reporting, approval and asset tracking, offer monitoring, first drafts of partner decks, briefs and email copy

Compliance and approvals

• Every co-marketing claim passes our review and the partner's. You build the templates and the rulebook so our side takes days, and you know each partner's process well enough to plan around it

What success looks like

Twelve months in:

• Every signed partnership is live in market within weeks of signing, with a calendar of placements the partner has committed to for the next two quarters

• Partner-sourced signups are a meaningful, measured share of new customers, tracked per partner, with CAC at or below what paid delivers

• At least two new co-marketing partners you found and qualified are signed and live

• The credit card launched with partner activations live on day one

• Partners get their numbers from us before they ask, and at least one has expanded its placement because of them

• A partner campaign goes from brief to live in weeks, not quarters, and the approvals rulebook is written

• Agents produce the partner reporting and the first drafts; your time goes to partners and what ships next

What we're looking for

• 4+ years in partner marketing, co-marketing, loyalty marketing or partnerships at a consumer brand, fintech, loyalty program, card issuer or telco

• You have taken a partnership from signed contract to live campaign and can show what it produced: signups, activations, points or revenue

• You have managed partners that were bigger and slower than you (a bank, an airline, a telco) and still shipped on a date

• You write well: the partner deck, the brief, the email a partner sends to its customers on our behalf, the one-pager that gets a bank's brand team to yes

• You are organized across many partners at once: calendars, approvals, assets, terms, deadlines, nothing dropped

• You own your numbers: you can read partner performance in BigQuery or equivalent, and you build your own reporting and automations (Zapier, n8n, Python, LLM APIs)

• You can be the single owner of a channel: no team under you, you run the campaigns yourself

Strong plus: loyalty program or card issuer co-marketing experience; Canadian consumer market experience; a regulated or claims-sensitive category (fintech, telco, insurance); French.

This probably isn't the role for you if

• You want to negotiate deals rather than make them work in market

• Partner marketing to you means an MDF budget and a partner portal

• A partner's six-week approval cycle is the reason the campaign slipped

• You need an agency or a team to get a campaign live

• AI on your resume means using ChatGPT for emails

• You can't say what your last partner campaign produced

Why join Chexy?

• Own the partner channel: Aeroplan and leading Canadian financial and telecom brands, one owner, no committee

• Partners are how Chexy grew: they have been part of the story since day one, and this seat turns the channel into a system

• Launch a credit card with partners behind it: our first card ships in Q1 2027

• Work the way partner marketing is going to work: agents on reporting and drafts, you on partners and decisions

• Work with the CMO and the founders: small team, fast decisions

• Equity: meaningful equity in a high-growth fintech

• Toronto office: we work in-office 5 days a week

How we hire

We keep our hiring process clear and human. You'll go through a mix of conversational interviews and practical discussions designed to show how you think, what you've built and how you work with others. Expect to walk us through a partnership you took from signed to live and what it produced, a partner approval you got unstuck and how, and an automation or agent you built that ran without you.

We use AI tools to help us organize and review applications; every decision about who we interview and who we hire is made by a person. This posting is for an existing vacancy. If you interview with us, we'll let you know within days of your last interview whether a decision has been made.

Chexy is an equal opportunity employer. If you require any accommodations or support during the hiring process, let us know and we'll do our best to help.

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Head of Growth Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one. You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.
What You Own
• The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
• The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
• Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
• The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
• Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
• What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
• The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.
What You Need
• Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
• 7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
• Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
• One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
• Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
• Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.
Please do not apply if
• Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
• You have only ever run one channel.
• All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
• What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.
Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

SysAid builds service management software used by 4,000+ organizations in 140 countries and more than 9 million people every day. We're recognized in Gartner's ITSM Magic Quadrant and by AWS as a Rising ISV Star, and generative AI sits at the centre of our product roadmap.

The Role

Our go-to-market stack is already connected to Claude through MCP, and we use it every day for forecasting, pipeline tracking, and account research. What we don't have yet is one person who owns that system end to end. That means two jobs at once. You'll set revenue strategy with the exec team: how a global sales org plans, forecasts, and sells. Then you'll build the workflows that carry it out. Most of that building happens directly in Claude, not as tickets in an ops queue.

What You Will Own:

1. Planning & Forecasting

• The forecast, capacity model, coverage, quota design, segmentation, and territories across regions.

• Tell leadership where growth will come from, where it won't, and what to shift as a result.

2. The Revenue Workflows

• Pipeline generation, enrichment, outreach, deal inspection, forecasting, and reporting.

• Decide what agents run and what people run, build it, keep it running, and replace it when something better ships.

3. Trust & Data Quality

• Evals, guardrails, and data quality, so a forecast an agent produced holds up in a board meeting.

• Know a workflow is drifting before a rep tells you.

4. Revenue Intelligence

• One view of performance from first touch through renewal and expansion.

• Surface risks and opportunities from Gong, Salesforce, and Snowflake before anyone has to ask.

5. The Stack

• Run it as one system. Add what earns its place and cut what doesn't.

What the Work Looks Like

• Late-quarter slippage shows up in one region. By the end of the week, an agent flags every deal without a next step and sends the list to the regional lead.

• Pipeline review prep that used to take a manager two hours is ready before they log on.

• A rep asks for a target list. Instead of building it, you fix the workflow so every rep can pull their own.

• You work through next year's territory design with the revenue leadership team, using a model you built that afternoon.

How We Work

Our footprint is global, and our team is lean, so leverage matters more than headcount. If a task repeats, it becomes a workflow. If a workflow matters, it gets measured. Some things should stay human, like a hard renewal conversation or a judgment call on comp, and we want you to have a clear view on where that line sits. You'll also bring the sales org along: share what you build, write the playbooks, and show people how to work this way themselves.

Requirements:

What You Bring

• You've built things with LLMs that a real team depends on, whether agents, MCP integrations, Claude projects or scripts, and you can walk us through what broke and how you fixed it.

• Strong revenue fundamentals: forecasting, capacity planning, comp, territories, and funnel management. Typically that's 5+ years in RevOps, sales ops, or strategy at a SaaS company, though what you've shipped matters more to us than tenure.

• You're comfortable in Salesforce and SQL (Snowflake or a similar warehouse), and you've used tools like Gong, Clay, Lemlist, or ZoomInfo, or can pick them up quickly.

• You can take a messy dataset and a skeptical executive and leave the room with a decision.

• You're based in Toronto or willing to relocate, and you'll be at Liberty Village four days a week.

How to Apply

Along with your resume, send us something you've built: a workflow, an agent, a repo or a short screen recording. A few lines on what it does and what you'd change next are plenty.

About Directive

At Directive, we’re a remote-first team of performance marketers obsessed with driving measurable growth for B2B SaaS and tech companies. We believe in data-backed strategy, radical accountability, and world-class execution across every channel — Paid Media, SEO & Content, CRO, Creative, and RevOps.

We’re building the next era of integrated marketing leadership, where creativity meets commercial discipline. Join us as we elevate how client strategy, retention, and growth are delivered at scale.

Role Summary

We’re hiring a Customer Marketing Manager to turn customer relationships into measurable retention, advocacy, and revenue growth. You’ll join Directive’s internal marketing team and build programs across three connected pillars: customer advocacy, lifecycle marketing, and expansion.

In this role, you’ll bring customer success stories to market, create campaigns that strengthen engagement and retention, and uncover opportunities to grow existing accounts. You’ll also reconnect with customer champions as they move between companies, activate referral and reference programs, and own targeted campaigns that support broader demand generation efforts. At Directive, everything ladders up to business outcomes, and your programs will be a major contributor to pipeline and revenue.

We’re looking for a marketer who can connect strategy with hands-on execution. You should be as comfortable interviewing a customer and writing a compelling case study as you are building a segmented campaign, managing marketing technology, and reporting on pipeline and revenue. If you love understanding what makes customers successful and translating that insight into growth, this role is built for you.

Key Responsibilities

•
Build and own the customer marketing strategy. Develop a coordinated plan across advocacy, lifecycle engagement, and expansion, with clear priorities, campaign calendars, and measurable business outcomes.

•
Own customer advocacy and social proof. Build a repeatable process for identifying customer advocates and turning their results into case studies, testimonials, reviews, references, and customer stories that support marketing and sales.

•
Lead customer lifecycle campaigns. Develop targeted communications and thoughtful gifting programs that reinforce the value of clients’ partnerships, introduce relevant services, and deepen engagement throughout the customer journey.

•
Turn past relationships into new opportunities. Use signal tracking software to identify job changes and other buying signals, then build targeted campaigns to reconnect with customer champions, past customers, and relevant contacts when new opportunities arise.

•
Support retention, expansion, and partner growth. Partner with client services and sales to identify engagement gaps, surface cross-sell and upsell opportunities, and build campaigns that support renewals and account growth. Use shared account insights and relationship signals to identify opportunities for referrals, introductions, and coordinated outreach between Directive and our partners.

•
Activate account overlap insights through the account mapping software and customer and partner overlap data to identify warm introductions and opportunities for coordinated account engagement.

•
Build and maintain a network of customer advocates who can speak to Directive’s impact. Match references to relevant sales opportunities, coordinate participation, and keep requests thoughtful and manageable for customers.

•
Build and grow the customer referral program, making it easy and rewarding for brand champions to introduce new business to Directive. Develop referral campaigns, manage incentives and follow-up, and track their contribution to pipeline and revenue.

•
Own targeted outreach and nurture campaigns that engage customer champions, past customers, and relevant prospects, while supporting additional demand generation programs as business priorities evolve.

Success Metrics (KPIs)

•
Net Revenue Retention (NRR)

•
Customer marketing-sourced and influenced expansion pipeline and revenue

•
Customer advocate participation and production of case studies, testimonials, and reviews

•
Customer reference participation and influence on sales opportunities

•
Lifecycle campaign engagement and conversion rates

Retention, renewal, and satisfaction outcomes are shared with client services; this role is accountable for the marketing programs that contribute to them.

Who You Are

Experience & Background

•
Proven experience in customer marketing, lifecycle marketing, or a closely related growth role, with ownership of programs tied to retention, advocacy, or expansion.

•
Experience marketing to B2B audiences, ideally within an agency, professional services business, or B2B SaaS company.

•
A track record of working on customer advocacy programs and producing compelling case studies, testimonials, or sales enablement content.

•
Hands-on experience developing segmented email campaigns and nurture programs, from audience selection and copywriting through execution and reporting.

•
Experience partnering with sales and client-facing teams to translate customer insight into campaigns and revenue opportunities.

•
Comfort working across Salesforce, HubSpot, marketing automation, and sales engagement platforms. Familiarity with signal tracking and account mapping software is a plus.

Core Competencies

•
Customer storytelling: You ask thoughtful questions, uncover meaningful results, and write clear, credible stories that make the customer’s success tangible.

•
Lifecycle strategy: You understand how audience, timing, and messaging work together to strengthen relationships and move people toward a relevant next step.

•
Commercial thinking: You connect marketing activity to retention, pipeline, and revenue, and prioritize work based on its potential business impact.

•
Operational execution: You build buy-in across the company, align leaders and teams around shared goals, and turn ideas into coordinated, repeatable programs.

•
Measurement and experimentation: You establish clear goals, interpret performance data, and test ways to improve results.

•
Cross-functional collaboration: You build trust with customers and internal teams, manage competing priorities, and keep work moving.

Cultural Fit & Traits

•
You take ownership of outcomes and follow through on the details.

•
You’re curious about customers’ businesses and motivated by helping them succeed.

•
You combine creative judgment with an analytical mindset.

•
You’re comfortable building repeatable processes while staying hands-on with execution.

•
You communicate directly, welcome feedback, and work independently in a remote environment.

•
You put the team’s success first. We work as one marketing team, with shared goals and flexible responsibilities. You take ownership of your work, jump in where you can make an impact, and collaborate across functions to drive pipeline and revenue together.

•
You use AI thoughtfully to support research, personalization, and execution while maintaining accuracy and a natural human voice.

What We Offer:

•
We have a set living wage at Directive; the actual salary may vary based on Directive's compensation practices, job related skills, and depth of experience.

•
Medical, dental, vision plans, disability, and life insurance coverage for you and your family that fit your lifestyle

•
Including a 100% employer-paid plan for you and a 50% employer contribution for your dependents (US, CAD, MX)

•
Benefits to Support the Whole Person:

•
Mental - Access to certified therapists through Spring Health, membership to Headspace

•
